title: In-Demand Career Options in Utah Without a Four-Year Degree
summary: Explore some of the top in-demand careers in Utah that may not require a bachelor’s degree, including skilled trade and technical career paths.
body_markdown:
Traditional university schooling doesn’t appeal to everyone. Maybe you want to save time and start earning and investing sooner. Perhaps you’re unsure about deciding on a major to dedicate four whole years of your life to, or more, considering one-fifth of bachelor’s degree students take even longer than four years to graduate, according to the[Education Data Initiative](https://educationdata.org/number-of-college-graduates) .


Thankfully, in Utah and around the country, there are in-demand careers that don’t require a 4-year degree. With[top skilled trades in demand](https://www.uti.edu/blog/education/skilled-trade-jobs-in-demand) , it’s possible to earn as much as jobs that require a traditional bachelor’s degree — in less time. From working for leading employers and manufacturers of top brands to growing your own business as an entrepreneur, you may have options to advance your career over time.


## H2: Key Takeaways


- Pursuing a career path that doesn’t require a 4-year degree means you can be ready to get to work more quickly and start earning and investing money earlier in your career.
- Many 4-year colleges will require students to take courses that don’t relate to their chosen field of study or desired career path. A technical school is shorter and focuses on teaching you the exact skills that are relevant to the job you want.
- In-demand jobs in Utah without a degree include automotive service technicians and mechanics, aircraft mechanics and service technicians, bus and truck mechanics, diesel engine specialists, HVACR technicians, industrial maintenance technicians, robotics and automation technicians, welders, cutters, solderers and brazers.


## Why Consider a Career That Doesn’t Require a Bachelor’s Degree?


There are a few reasons to consider pursuing a career track that doesn’t require a 4-year bachelor’s degree. If any of the following resonates, it may be worth exploring non-university options.


### You want to be ready to start working more quickly.


A 4-year degree program will, like its title suggests, require *at least* four years of schooling. A 4-year degree program can take even longer, if a student:


- Changes their major during the program.
- Experiences a life event that requires taking time off, such as an injury or needing to leave school to take care of a family member.
- Needs to take time off and/or decrease their course load in order to work and earn money to pay for school.
- Transfers schools and needs to make up credit requirements.
- Fails a course and needs to retake it in order to fulfill degree requirements.


These are just a few causes for a delay in a 4-year university program. Every semester in school means time away from working, earning money and having the potential to save and invest for the future.


If you want to be ready to start working and earning money more quickly, a shorter-term program like one offered at our[trade school in Salt Lake City](https://www.uti.edu/locations/utah/salt-lake-city) can prepare you to enter the workforce sooner.1


### You aren’t passionate about a traditional classroom environment.


In a traditional 4-year university, most of the college courses students take have nothing to do with their major. According to a 2026 report by[Forbes,](https://www.forbes.com/sites/scottwhite/2023/10/01/are-the-liberal-arts-dead--no-just-changed/) up to three-fourths of courses students take aren’t part of their majors, but instead are focused on liberal arts, like language and social sciences.


These types of classes often require you to sit in a classroom or log in online to listen to a lecture. For students who prefer hands-on work compared to lecture-style learning, a 4-year college can be challenging to get through.


A technical school, like our[automotive technician school in Salt Lake City](https://www.uti.edu/locations/utah/salt-lake-city/automotive) or[welding school in Salt Lake City](https://www.uti.edu/locations/utah/salt-lake-city/welding) , is shorter, while providing a curriculum that relates directly to the career you want to pursue. You won’t have to take required classes that you’re not interested in or will never use again. This makes learning more engaging and relevant to the career you’re interested in.


### You want more autonomy.


If a job forces you to have a 4-year degree, what other requirements will there be? A skilled trades education gives you the know-how to work for a variety of employers, including yourself, if you want to start your own business. What’s more, a[2025 study by the Federal Reserve Bank of Minneapolis](https://www.inc.com/bruce-crumley/why-entrepreneurs-earn-more-than-salaried-employees/91248340) found small business owners saw faster rates of income growth compared to employees of other companies. Being your own boss gives you the power to make your own career decisions and could provide the opportunity to earn more.


For those who aren’t interested in playing workplace politics and climbing the corporate ladder, a job outside the world of 4-year degree requirements might be more lucrative. Your time is one of your most valuable assets, so saving time and earning money faster may make more sense for some career seekers.


## Top Jobs in Utah Without a Bachelor’s Degree


Start working, and start earning, more quickly, with a Utah job that doesn’t require a bachelor’s degree. The following jobs that don't require a 4-year degree are in demand in Utah and throughout the country.


*Note: Keep in mind that salary depends on several factors, including experience, employer, demand and cost of living in the area.*


### Automotive & diesel


According to the U.S.[Bureau of Labor Statistics](https://www.bls.gov/oes/current/oes493023.htm) (BLS), the median annual salary for automotive service technicians and mechanics in the United States was **$50,620** in May 2025.25 This means half of automotive technicians earned more and half earned less.


According to the[BLS](https://www.bls.gov/oes/tables.htm) , the median annual salary for bus and truck mechanics and diesel engine specialists in the United States was **$61,770** in May 2025.29 This means half of diesel technicians earned more and half earned less.


### HVACR


According to the[BLS](https://www.bls.gov/oes/current/oes499021.htm) , the median annual salary for HVACR technicians in the United States was $61,010 in May 2025.58 This means half earned more and half earned less.


### Welding & industrial careers


According to the[BLS](https://www.bls.gov/oes/current/oes514121.htm) , the median annual salary for welders, cutters, solderers and brazers in the United States was **$53,750** in May 2025.26 This means half of welders earned more and half earned less.


According to the[BLS](https://www.bls.gov/oes/current/oes514121.htm) , the median annual salary for industrial maintenance technicians in the United States was **$64,520** in May 2025.60 This means half earned more and half earned less.


According to the[BLS](https://www.bls.gov/oes/current/oes514121.htm) , the median annual salary for robotics and automation technicians in the United States was **$73,900** in May 2025.59 This means half earned more and half earned less.


### Aviation & other technical careers


According to the[BLS](https://www.bls.gov/oes/current/oes514121.htm) , the median annual salary for aviation maintenance technicians in the United States was **$79,870** in May 2025.57 This means half earned more and half earned less. Career options may be limited without an FAA-issued mechanic certificate, and salaries may be lower.[Aviation trade school](https://www.uti.edu/locations/utah/salt-lake-city/aviation) can prepare you to test for FAA Airframe and Powerplant certification.79,128


## What Affects Earnings in Utah?


In Utah, there are a number of factors that can impact how much someone can earn in a given career path. While the above salary figures are national estimates, consider these variables when estimating salary earnings in Utah.


- **Experience:** Hands-on training and experience may factor into salary offerings. An apprenticeship or in-the-field experience can impact earning potential.
- **Employer:** An employer’s earnings, clientele and demand can impact how they compensate employees.
- **Career demand:** Employers with worker shortages and employers that are experiencing high growth may be more likely to offer competitive compensation.
- **Cost of living:** Generally, employers will consider factors like cost of living when determining salary. For example, employers in an area with a high cost of living may offer higher salaries compared to employers in an area with a low cost of living.


These factors can impact entry-level earnings, as well as help you accelerate earnings over time. The more experience you accrue and business you can help bring to and retain at your employer, the more your earning potential can grow.


Entrepreneurs who start their own businesses can also have different earning trajectories, as they have more influence over their earning potential.


## How Trade School Can Prepare You for a Technical Career


Trade school can prepare you for a technical career in many ways. According to the BLS, some of the careers mentioned in this post require a postsecondary non-degree award, like you can earn at our[Utah technical school](https://www.uti.edu/locations/utah) . A technical school teaches you the exact skills you need to pursue an entry-level position in your chosen field. The hands-on education you get at a technical school can set you up to get to work right away.152


It’s helpful to learn technical skills in a safe, hands-on environment with expert instructor support. You’re able to get practical advice, learn on equipment used in the field, and feel confident as you develop your skills.


With a diploma or associate of occupational studies degree in hand, depending on the program you choose, you can obtain career-advancing certifications and show employers you have the knowledge needed to succeed on the job.


Our trade school in Utah is shorter than a 4-year university, sometimes only taking nine months to 51 weeks to complete. You don’t have to take courses that don’t relate to your field. You can graduate more quickly and be ready to get to work faster in a field you’re passionate about.1


Whether you’re about to graduate high school, you’re already working and want to change careers, or someone you care about is considering their career options, technical school can open up a world of possibilities. There are careers in demand that don’t require attending a 4-year college.


## Jobs in Utah Without a 4-Year Degree FAQs


### What jobs that don't require a bachelor’s degree are in-demand in Utah?


Some of the in-demand jobs in Utah that don’t require a bachelor’s degree include automotive technician, diesel technician, welder, HVACR technician, robotics and automation technician, industrial maintenance technician, and aviation maintenance technician.


### What in-demand skilled trade careers are available in Salt Lake City?


In Salt Lake City, in-demand skilled trade careers include HVAC technician, automotive technician, aviation maintenance technician, diesel technician and welder.


### What training is needed for in-demand trade careers in Utah?


It depends on the position. According to the BLS, positions like HVAC technician and installer, automotive service technician and mechanic, and aircraft and avionics equipment mechanic and technician require a post-secondary non-degree award. For some jobs, a post-secondary non-degree award like a diploma or associate degree can increase earning potential.
